references.text: The Mosaic law concerning a woman with bleeding (a flow of blood) – the background for her uncleanness and social isolation mentioned in Luke 8:43.
The parallel account in Matthew about the woman who had been bleeding for twelve years and touched Jesus' cloak.
The parallel account in Mark, which gives more details about the woman, including that she had suffered much under many doctors and spent all she had without getting better.
Job complains about doctors who are worthless ('useless physicians'), reflecting the woman's experience that no doctor could heal her.
King Asa sought doctors instead of the Lord in his illness – a contrast to the woman who finally turned to Jesus after the doctors had failed.
